required_changes: source_encoding.py:17,26,29,30 uses bare `assert` for its gates: choice/conditional uniqueness, the single divineName, and the paired '(' / ')' tails. Under `python -O` these checks disappear and the code edits text with nothing checking it. Replace each with an explicit `raise ValueError(...)`, as every other gate in apply_source_encoding already does.

source_encoding.py:29 inner_condition: `preceding=parent[idx-1]` wraps to the last child when the divineName is the first child (idx==0). It then strips '(' from the wrong node's tail, or only stops at an assert that -O removes. Require idx>0. Also, the divineName is searched across the whole parent, not inside the outer scope. Require that it sits strictly between `cond` and that condition's own `j:endConditional` (the one whose target is '#'+cond xml:id), so a nested Name pair can never be placed outside, or across, the outer scope it is meant to nest in.

source_encoding.py:15 quietly skips any interpretation whose `stem` differs from unit['stem'], and :16/:25 treat every kind other than 'alternate' as 'optional'. Such a rule is still serialized into unit_review_text, so a reviewer can approve a payload claiming an interpretation that is never applied. Raise when a rule's stem does not match or its kind is not in {'alternate','optional'}. Also validate per-rule keys, and for the other directives the keys of each item and fragment, against an allow-list. A misspelled `inner_condition` or `missing_opener` is currently either ignored through r.get or raises a bare KeyError, and neither is a clear gate.

build.py identity validation (urn_strings over unit['languages'], wording_selection, conditions, citations, source_order, expanded_order) never walks unit['source_encoding']. A new condition URN brought in only by source_encoding, such as `inner_condition` (e.g. .../additional_couplet/divine_name), the `condition` in a rule, or `continuous_quotation_chapter.corresp`, is never checked against the registry for canonical or registered form. The prior blocking defect was exactly a misspelled condition URN. Add `urn_strings(unit.get('source_encoding', {}))` to the checked set.
material_risks: Several directives change characters but have no word-preservation check after they run. alternate `colon_after_choice` adds ':' with no check that the colon was removed from the readings, or that the tail does not already begin with ':'. inner_condition deletes '(' and ')'. remove_prayer_footnote_marker swaps `printed` for any `text` without confirming the difference is only the marker. Only reference_terminators_outside_container and commentary_pages compare text before and after. A single final check would close all of these: printed_text(body) before versus after, with only the approved delimiter, siglum and marker deltas allowed. These edits are approved semantics today, but the code does not stop a bad config value.

continuous_quotation_chapter (source_encoding.py:98-108) removes every chapter milestone in the body, including any that carry @corresp, and overwrites @type on every seg[@source], including types set by source_type. That throws away identities and types without saying so. `paragraphs[0].insert(0, marker)` also leaves any existing paragraphs[0].text in front of the new chapter opener, outside the chapter. The only gate is the paragraph count. Recommend asserting that the removed milestones had no @corresp other than context['corresp'], that existing seg types are absent or 'quotation', and that paragraphs[0].text is blank.

The inner Divine Name conditional's xml:id comes from the outer id (`<stem>_optional_<segment>_<fragment>_<n>` + '_divine_name'), which depends on position. Today no annotation targets it, so this is acceptable. Annotation targets that are configured (choice xml_id, `<xml_id>_source_error`) are stable. Do not point future notes at the positional ids.

The commentary_pages tei:pb elements sit inside standOff notes and use plain ed='1965'. They are not context-qualified like the body pb rewrite at build.py:758-763, and the exporter may count them as page events alongside the body's own pb for the same page. Schema validity alone does not rule out doubled page markers in the output.

documentary_order declarations (build.py:1105-1111): a section whose only children are j:declare and j:endDeclare is not caught by the empty-section removal check at :1114, which only looks for conditional/endConditional. An empty declare pair would be left behind. Nothing triggers this now, but it is easy to guard against.

The review hash covers the serialized config, not the code in source_encoding.py. Changing what a directive does will not invalidate existing reviews. This is true of all importer code, but it matters more here because each directive has its own fixed meaning.

notes: The overall approach is sound. apply_source_encoding runs last in unit_document, only when there is a config for that language. Its top-level directive allow-list rejects unknown keys (and is tested). The whole config is serialized with sort_keys into unit_review_text, so any change in interpretation invalidates the unit review hash; test_interpretation_change_invalidates_review_payload shows this while languages stay unchanged.

The missing-opener handling is correct. The anchor goes right after the opening j:conditional, takes over its tail so no text moves, and the standOff note targets the stable `<xml_id>_source_error`, so the note is kept or dropped along with the scope. An alternate annotation targets the configured choice xml:id, which is also stable.

reference_terminators_outside_container fails closed. It only moves a bare stanza milestone that is the last child of an l or p and has a blank tail. Anything else, such as a closing endConditional after it, raises. It also compares printed_text before and after. The regression confirms that outer=false no longer swallows the next stanza, and that the terminators end up as children of lg.

commentary_pages also fails closed. The note's paragraph must have no children and its text must equal the concatenated fragments exactly, and itertext is compared again after the pb elements are inserted.

Local documentary declarations wrap only the recursive documentary_order call for that section. Their ids are unique within each generated document, and their feature URNs are already checked against the registry through source_order.

The required changes are small and local, and none affects the 11 integrated bodies already reviewed, provided they are still produced unchanged afterwards. Approval would cover importer code only, not assembly, export or batch acceptance. I made no edits.
